facts.label: Going to e will
facts.sub: Use going to para planos: I’m going to have a party. Use will para ofertas e opiniões: I’ll bring a cake. I think it’ll be fun.

facts.label: Going to
facts.sub: Para falar de planos, use am/is/are going to + verbo: I’m going to have a party. We’re going to watch the fireworks. Use quando o plano já está na sua cabeça.

facts.label: Will
facts.sub: Para oferecer ajuda, use I’ll + verbo: I’ll bring a cake. I’ll take photos. A forma curta I’ll é muito comum na fala.

pages.title: A party room · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Tuesday evening in a busy party room in Auckland. Colorful lights hang from the ceiling. Max puts chairs around a table. His friend Cora comes in with a bag. The new year starts in two days. Cora asks about the plans.
“Hi, Max! What are you going to do on New Year’s Eve?” says Cora. “I’m going to have a party at my house.” says Max. “Nice! Who is going to come?” says Cora.

items.why: Com she, o verbo leva -s: makes.
Com we, a forma base: watch.

solo: Aluno responde; você explica o porquê.

answers: Yesterday I ___. → had
She ___ every day. → makes
He is ___ now. → bringing
We ___ every day. → watch

After will, use the base verb.
